title: Reed’s conjecture
formal: Does every nonempty finite simple undirected graph \(G\) satisfy \[\chi(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G)}{2}\right\rceil?\] The quantification is over every number of vertices and every edge set, with no restriction on maximum degree or graph class.
definitions: For an integer \(n\geq1\), let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(E\) be any set of two-element subsets of \(V\). Thus \(G=(V,E)\) has no loops or parallel edges, and an edge has no direction. Vertices \(u,v\) are adjacent exactly when \(\{u,v\}\in E\). A proper \(k\)-colouring, for an integer \(k\geq1\), is a function \(c:V\to\{1,\ldots,k\}\) with \(c(u)\ne c(v)\) for every edge; colours need not all be used. The chromatic number \(\chi(G)\) is the least such \(k\), which exists since \(k=n\) always suffices. Write \(d_G(v)=|\{u\in V:\{u,v\}\in E\}|\) and \(\Delta(G)=\max_{v\in V}d_G(v)\). A clique is a subset \(S\subseteq V\) whose distinct vertices are pairwise adjacent, and \(\omega(G)=\max\{|S|:S\text{ is a clique}\}\). Both maxima are over finite sets, and a singleton is a clique. The ceiling \(\lceil x\rceil\) is the least integer at least the real number \(x\); the division by two in the displayed bound is real division before rounding. Disconnected graphs, isolated vertices and all nonempty edgeless graphs are included; the latter have \(\chi=\omega=1\) and \(\Delta=0\). Labelling the vertices imposes no structural restriction. One may also include the empty graph with \(\chi=\omega=\Delta=0\), for which the inequality is immediate. This is an existence question about one ordinary proper colouring per graph, with no input algorithm, running-time, randomness, list assignment or recolouring requirement.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete, mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal displayed inequality, or a complete Lean-checked refutation: a specified integer \(n\geq1\), a specified finite simple graph \(G\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and a proof that \(\chi(G)>\lceil(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G))/2\rceil\). In the negative case the exact graph parameters, or certified bounds that imply this strict inequality, must be established; in particular, merely exhibiting a clique gives a lower bound on \(\omega(G)\), whereas an upper bound on the right-hand side is needed for a refutation. Equivalently, the proof may certify the absence of any proper colouring with the specified threshold number of colours. A positive proof must include every maximum degree and every graph size, including bounded-degree cases. The target is the exact universal proposition, not an estimate of an optimal coefficient, so no numerical approximation tolerance replaces it. An additive error, a smaller clique coefficient, a theorem for only sufficiently large maximum degree, or success for a restricted graph class does not meet the criterion unless the full statement follows. The existence proof need not give a polynomial-time colouring algorithm.
why: A defining question about how a local degree constraint and a global clique obstruction jointly control ordinary graph colouring. A positive resolution would give a sharp universal guarantee for partitioning vertices into independent colour classes, while a counterexample would reveal a colouring obstruction beyond this proposed relationship among three basic graph parameters. Its significance is structural even without an efficient algorithm for finding the guaranteed colouring.

importance.reason: A defining universal conjecture linking three basic graph parameters, with sharp examples and broad influence on colouring theory and its algorithmic methods.

progress.text: Reed states the exact half-average conjecture and proves a universal interpolation with some positive clique coefficient. The original statements are restated as Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 in the checked September 2026 primary revision.
Bonamy–Kelly–Nelson–Postle establish the logarithmic-ratio small-clique bound; the checked author preprint is dated 2 March 2018, and the journal article appears in November 2022.
The final published Hurley–de Joannis de Verclos–Kang version states the large-degree \(0.119\) interpolation and records the dated dependency qualification and \(0.113\) alternative in Remark 3.1.

De Meyer and coauthors post a distinct Kempe-recolouring conjecture with coefficient \(1/3\); their odd-hole-free result guarantees recolouring with a strict threshold inequality, not the remaining equality case. This remains the only listed arXiv version on 14 September 2026.

Kawarabayashi–Picasarri-Arrieta v4 retains the undirected target as Conjecture 1.1 and the stronger directed half-average as Conjecture 1.6; Theorem 1.7 proves only a positive-coefficient directed interpolation. A shorter version was published at SODA 2025.

Its proved directed interpolation, the large-degree 0.119/0.113 results, and the checked Kempe-recolouring theorem do not imply the missing universal half-average. Bounded later-work searches found no full matching resolution; this is dated primary-source evidence of openness, not an independent proof of current status or verification of every cited theorem.

context_blocks.text: The basic bounds are \(\omega(G)\leq\chi(G)\leq\Delta(G)+1\): a clique requires different colours at all its vertices, while the upper bound follows from the usual greedy-colouring theorem. Reed asks whether the rounded average of these two scales is always an upper bound. The conjecture concerns the global partition into independent sets, meaning vertex sets containing no edge, rather than a separate choice of colours within each neighbourhood.

The ceiling matters. A five-cycle has \(\Delta=\omega=2\) and \(\chi=3\), whereas the unrounded average is \(5/2\). Complete graphs attain the proposed rounded bound as well. These examples distinguish the exact statement from an asymptotic estimate with an unspecified additive constant.

The coefficient \(1/2\) cannot be increased in a universal interpolation \(\lceil(1-\varepsilon)(\Delta+1)+\varepsilon\omega\rceil\). Replace each vertex of a five-cycle by a clique of size \(t\geq1\), and put all edges between two replacement cliques exactly when their original cycle vertices are adjacent. This graph has \(5t\) vertices, \(\Delta=3t-1\), \(\omega=2t\), and no independent set larger than two vertices, hence \(\chi\geq\lceil5t/2\rceil\). For any fixed \(\varepsilon>1/2\), the proposed interpolation would be smaller than this lower bound for sufficiently large \(t\). This explicitly defined clique blowup is the example intended in the source; its description there as a Cartesian product is inaccurate.

Reed proved that some universal \(\varepsilon>0\) does give the weaker bound \(\chi(G)\leq\lceil(1-\varepsilon)(\Delta(G)+1)+\varepsilon\omega(G)\rceil\) for every graph. Thus a saving proportional to the gap between degree plus one and clique number is known; the unresolved target is the sharp half-average. The September 2026 digraph paper restates the original conjecture and this result as Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2, respectively.

Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos and Kang give \(\chi(G)\leq\lceil0.881(\Delta(G)+1)+0.119\omega(G)\rceil\) when \(\Delta(G)\geq\Delta_0\) for a universal threshold \(\Delta_0\). Their published 2022 Remark 3.1 explicitly says that an ingredient attributed to Delcourt and Postle had not then completed peer review; it also records an alternative published ingredient giving coefficients \(0.887\) and \(0.113\). This is a dated qualification about the 2022 argument, not a claim about the present review status of that ingredient. Neither variant provides coefficient \(1/2\), and the stated large-degree restriction must be retained.

Bonamy, Kelly, Nelson and Postle prove a different kind of improvement, \(\chi(G)=O(\Delta\sqrt{\ln\omega/\ln\Delta})\), for graphs of maximum degree at most \(\Delta\) and clique number at most \(\omega\), in the large-\(\Delta\) regime with \(\omega\geq2\). The implicit constant is universal. This becomes substantially smaller than the degree bound when \(\ln\omega/\ln\Delta\) is small; it does not give the exact half-average for every parameter range. The theorem in the 2018 author preprint also bounds the list-chromatic number, where every vertex has its own list of allowed colours.

A Kempe change swaps two colours on one connected component of the subgraph induced by those colours. The 2025 recolouring paper studies whether every pair of proper \(k\)-colourings is connected by a sequence of such changes. Its general conjectured clique coefficient is \(1/3\), due to obstructions to moving between colourings; this is a separate property from the existence of one colouring. For odd-hole-free graphs, meaning graphs with no induced odd cycle of length at least five, Theorem 4 guarantees recolourability above a local threshold, and in particular for \(k>\lceil(\omega+\Delta+1)/2\rceil\). The strict inequality leaves the equality case open in that recolouring question.

The September 2026 revision of Kawarabayashi and Picasarri-Arrieta replaces undirected colour classes by acyclic colour classes in a digraph, where acyclic means containing no directed cycle, including no two-cycle of opposite arcs. In the symmetric digraph obtained by replacing each edge by both opposite arcs, this is exactly ordinary proper colouring. Their proposed directed half-average bound therefore implies Reed’s conjecture, but their proved general interpolation has only some positive coefficient. Conjecture 1.1 of this revision still lists the full undirected half-average as open.

sentences: Reed’s conjecture asks whether every finite simple undirected graph has a proper colouring using at most the rounded average of maximum degree plus one and clique number.
The card fixes all graph parameters and includes disconnected graphs, isolated vertices and every maximum degree.
Acceptance requires a complete Lean-checked proof of the universal exact bound or a certified finite counterexample, without requiring an efficient colouring algorithm.

The sharp interpolation would relate local degree restrictions to the global need for independent colour classes, and clique blowups of a five-cycle explain why the half coefficient cannot be increased.
The checked September 2026 primary revision still states the target as open; known smaller-coefficient and restricted recolouring results have different scopes.
